title: Integrated MF-C tool — macro-fiscal and climate
subtitle: built from the Global Fiscal Indicators dashboard (v1.2 panel) and the mitigation investment needs models (v1.1 workbook, NMIM v0.2).

readme_replace.What this is: The integrated macro-fiscal climate (MF-C) tool. It puts the Global Fiscal Indicators dashboard and the mitigation investment needs models on one country page: what a country's net zero programme needs and costs, beside whether it can pay for it, build it, and finance it. More modules will be added. The is_ccdr column flags the 98 economies with a published Country Climate and Development Report.
readme_replace.How it is organised: Thirteen blocks, in reading order. Four ASSESSMENT blocks carry the diagnosis: fiscal space, delivery, cost of capital, and financing. Three CONTEXT blocks explain it: fossil revenue in the budget, fossil trade and extraction, and power generation. Two INVESTMENT blocks give the need: Investment 1 (2030 snapshot, by sector and cost-of-capital lens) and Investment 2 (who pays, and the path to 2050). They read High / Medium / Low, like the Context blocks. Four APPENDIX blocks - fuel pricing, power market regulation, macro-model inputs and the integrated scenario - are reference detail in grey and carry no block verdict.

readme_add: Investment 1 and 2 are MODEL OUTPUT, not data, from InvestmentNeeds/: the v1.1 workbook (195 economies, 2030, group totals allocated to countries, 2023 prices) and the national model NMIM v0.2 (186 countries, 2024-2050, 2024 prices). Their year is the scenario year. Everything is in % of the model's own GDP for that year, so the two can be compared but will not match: v1.1 allocates IHLEG and IEA-IFC totals, NMIM builds up from stocks. See InvestmentNeeds/README.md and NMIM_Method_v0_2.md.

Incremental cost = annual capital charge on incremental investment less fuel and operating savings (lens c also less local co-benefits); negative = net saving. Lens (a) uses the market WACC, (b) and (c) the World Bank 6% rate. The cost-of-capital penalty is the extra capital charge on total investment at the market rate over 6% (negative where market capital is cheaper). Who pays splits NMIM's net zero investment into P1 pure public, P2 regulated utility, P3 contracted revenue, P4 viability gap and P5 pure private; the direct budget need is P1 plus the public 30% of P4.

Appendix D's budget need is the incremental budget need from NMIM, as passed through MacroFiscalModels; Investment 2's is the budget need of the whole net zero programme. Use Investment 2 for size and composition, Appendix D for what it does to the budget and debt.
